subject: humpback whale
title: A Humpback Whale Turned Up 8,106 Miles From Where It Was Seen

scenes.text: A whale seen off Colombia turned up next in Africa.
Humpbacks migrate north and south. They rarely cross oceans sideways.
A male photographed off Colombia in twenty thirteen surfaced off Zanzibar in twenty twenty-two.
At least eight thousand one hundred miles apart. The farthest sightings ever recorded for the species.
Every humpback's tail pattern is unique. A citizen science photo site matched the two.
Why go? Probably love. Off Colombia and off Africa, he was in the same place: a group chasing a female.

description:
A male humpback whale photographed off Colombia in 2013 and 2017 was spotted off Zanzibar in 2022, at least 8,106 miles (13,046 km) away, the longest distance between sightings ever recorded for the species.
His tail photos were matched on the Happywhale database. Researchers think mating competition, shifting food or climate change may explain the trip.
What do you think pushed him that far?
first_comment: The old record was a female humpback that went about 6,100 miles from Brazil to Madagascar. This male beat it by about 2,000 miles. Where would you swim with that much range?
